# Why do blind boxes turn uncertainty into repeat purchase behavior?

This published research examines the consumer-psychology mechanisms behind the popularity of POP MART's blind-box model in China. The paper connects uncertainty, scarcity, emotional reward, social influence, and brand strategy through three established psychological frameworks.

## Research question

The study asks why POP MART's blind-box products can motivate repeat purchasing when consumers do not know exactly which item they will receive.

The analysis focuses on four connected mechanisms:

- **uncertainty** around the item received,
- **scarcity** and limited-edition design,
- **emotional reward** when a desired or rare item appears,
- and **social reinforcement** through online communities and brand culture.

## Analytical framework

::: {.stage-grid}
::: {.stage-card}
### Prospect Theory

Blind-box purchases take place under uncertainty. The framework helps explain why the possibility of obtaining a rare item can influence perceived value and decision-making even when the outcome is not guaranteed.
:::

::: {.stage-card}
### Cognitive Dissonance

After purchase, consumers may rationalize disappointing outcomes, continue collecting, or seek another purchase to reduce the tension between expectation and result.
:::

::: {.stage-card}
### Maslow's Hierarchy

Collectibles can serve more than functional needs. Identity, belonging, social recognition, and self-expression help explain why community participation can strengthen attachment to a brand.
:::
:::

## From psychology to business strategy

The paper does not treat consumer psychology as an isolated academic topic. It connects psychological mechanisms to specific commercial choices.

### Scarcity and limited editions

Scarcity can increase perceived value and urgency, especially when consumers believe a desired design may become difficult to obtain.

### IP collaborations and product design

Distinctive characters and collaborations can strengthen emotional attachment and give customers reasons to continue engaging with the product ecosystem.

### Social media and community culture

Online sharing, unboxing content, collecting communities, and peer discussion can reinforce consumer choice and brand loyalty beyond the initial transaction.

## Managerial implications

::: {.skill-grid}
::: {.skill-card}
### Product innovation

Keep the product experience novel enough to sustain discovery while avoiding a portfolio that depends only on artificial scarcity.
:::

::: {.skill-card}
### Customer experience

Design the purchase and collecting journey around emotional engagement, community participation, and repeat interaction—not only the moment of sale.
:::

::: {.skill-card}
### Brand growth

Use IP, community, and global market adaptation to build a durable brand rather than relying on one short-lived collectible trend.
:::
:::

## What this research demonstrates

This publication represents an earlier part of my work at the intersection of **finance, marketing, consumer behavior, and business strategy**. It demonstrates the ability to translate academic theory into a structured explanation of real commercial behavior and then derive practical recommendations from that framework.
